name: Zoho CRM
one_liner: Cloud CRM for sales pipelines, contacts, and automations, with a public REST API.

one_liner.note: Zoho CRM product site for the sales CRM platform.

auth.note: OAuth2.0 requests are usually authenticated with an access token, which is passed as bearer token. Send the token in the HTTP authorization header as Zoho-oauthtoken {access_token}.

Before you get started with authorization and make any calls using the Zoho CRM APIs, you need to register your application with Zoho CRM. You will receive the client credentials such as Client ID and Client Secret.

access.note: Registration is done in the Zoho Developer Console by choosing a client type and clicking CREATE NOW; no sales review is required to obtain client credentials.
Free Edition includes API access, with 5,000 credits in a 24-hour window and a concurrency limit of 5 calls per user/app.

api_surface.note: Official Zoho CRM API v8 HTTP documentation for calling Zoho CRM APIs.
Use the api_domain from the token response to make HTTP API calls to Zoho CRM.

mcp.note: Zoho CRM provides these as pre-built MCP servers, so you don't need to build, host, or maintain any infrastructure. They work with Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code, and Windsurf.

verdict.note: Public docs and a self-serve Developer Console registration path exist, so a toolkit can be built today.

notes: The Client Secret issued at app registration is the OAuth client_secret, not a standalone API key for the CRM API. Zoho CRM Functions can optionally expose REST endpoints with a zapikey; that is function-endpoint security, not a documented auth method for the CRM API itself. MCP actions consume the same API credits. A customer org admin or user must complete the OAuth consent for their CRM org.
label_notes: oauth2 only. Did not list api_key for the dashboard client secret, per the clarified rubric. Free Edition documents API credits, so access is self_serve.

name: Help Scout
one_liner: Shared inbox and help desk for email, chat, and knowledge bases, with public HTTP APIs.

one_liner.note: Help Scout marketing site for the shared inbox and help desk product.

auth.note: This is an HTTPS-only API and it uses OAuth 2.0 authorization, implementing Authorization Code and Client Credential flows. Create an OAuth2 application under Your Profile > My apps.
Docs API authentication is based on API keys. The API key is passed via HTTP Basic Authentication and goes in the username field. A dummy password, such as X, goes in the password field.

access.note: Each paid Help Scout plan has API access. The Free plan does not include access to the API or integrations.

When you sign up for a free trial of the Standard or Plus plan, you'll get 15 days to take all of the plan's features for a test drive — no credit card required. API access is listed as a Standard, Plus, and Pro feature.

api_surface.note: Inbox API 2.0 is an HTTPS-only API with OAuth 2 authentication running at https://api.helpscout.net/v2. It uses JSON for requests and responses.
The Docs API is an HTTPS JSON API at https://docsapi.helpscout.net/v1 for collections and articles.

mcp.note: Help Scout MCP gives AI assistants official access to Help Scout data. Set the remote MCP server URL to https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp. Available on Standard, Plus, and Pro plans.

verdict.note: Public Inbox API docs and a self-serve path to create an OAuth2 application exist, including during a Standard or Plus trial.

notes: Inbox API auth is OAuth 2.0; the My Apps application secret is an OAuth client_secret, not a standalone API key. The Docs API uses a separate profile API key sent via HTTP Basic as the username with a dummy password; under the clarified rubric that remains api_key, not basic. Light Users and some custom-permission roles lack API access. MCP is read-only and also requires API access on the account.
label_notes: Listed oauth2 (Inbox API) plus api_key (Docs API). Did not add basic for the Docs key-via-Basic transport. Access is self_serve because a no-card Standard/Plus trial includes API features, even though the standing Free plan does not.

name: Vonage
one_liner: Communications platform with public APIs for SMS, voice, video, verify, and messaging.

one_liner.note: Vonage API Developer home for the communications platform APIs.

auth.note: When you create a Vonage account, an API key and secret will be created for you. A number of newer Vonage APIs require authentication using an API key and secret sent Base64 encoded in the Authorization header as Basic base64(API_KEY:API_SECRET).
Vonage APIs also support JSON Web Tokens signed with an application private key. Messages supports both JWT and Basic authentication; for most use-cases Vonage recommends JWT Authentication.

access.note: When you create a Vonage account, an API key and secret will be created for you. These are located in your account settings in the Vonage Dashboard.
Getting started documentation for signing up and authenticating Vonage API requests with Basic Authentication or JWTs.

api_surface.note: Official authentication docs list many HTTP APIs (SMS, Messages, Voice, Verify, Numbers, and others) and how to call them.

mcp.note: The Vonage Server API Bindings MCP Server, also known as the Tooling MCP Server, is installed with npx @vonage/vonage-mcp-server-api-bindings and uses application and API credentials as environment variables.

verdict.note: Public docs and dashboard-issued API credentials exist on signup, so a toolkit can be built today.

notes: API key and secret sent as HTTP Basic are still api_key, not a separate basic method, because the credentials are a key and secret rather than a user username/password. JWT application keys are jwt_service_account and are recommended for Messages, Voice, and similar APIs. SIP digest auth is a special case for SIP trunking, not a general API method. Creating an application and keys happens in the customer's Vonage account.
label_notes: Did not list basic for key:secret-via-Basic, per the clarified rubric. primary_auth is jwt_service_account because official auth docs recommend JWT for most use-cases.

name: Pinterest
one_liner: Visual discovery platform with a REST API for pins, boards, catalogs, and ads.

one_liner.note: Connect your app to the Pinterest API and follow the Connect app steps.

auth.note: Pinterest API services are only available to authenticated and authorized users. Make sure your API requests on a user's behalf include a current access token. You provide your app ID and client secret as credentials when requesting an OAuth access token.

access.note: Submit your request for trial access. Application requests are reviewed by Pinterest. You will receive an email notification after your app has been reviewed, letting you know whether it was approved or denied access. If approved for Trial access, you can find your unique app ID and app secret.
If approved for API use, your app receives Trial access. Upgrading to Standard access requires a further review, including a video of the OAuth flow.

api_surface.note: Official docs describe calling Pinterest API services with OAuth access tokens after app registration.
Trial and Standard access cover reading and creating Pins, boards, catalogs, ads, and audiences over the API.

mcp.note: The official Pinterest MCP landing page says 'Be the first to know when it launches' and is still framed as not generally available, even though a sample config mentions https://api.pinterest.com/mcp. Treated as a coming-soon mention, so mcp_status is none.

verdict.note: A documented API exists, but usable credentials require Pinterest to review and approve a trial-access request first.

notes: The app secret issued after approval is the OAuth client_secret, not a standalone API key. There is no self-serve personal-token path; even Trial access is granted only after a vendor review, so access is gated_partner rather than self_serve. Standard access is a second review. The official MCP page advertises a future server and shows a sample URL, but still says it has not launched; that mention is recorded here and mcp_status is none.
label_notes: Hard call on MCP: official marketing/docs page includes a server URL snippet but explicitly says 'when it launches'. Applied the rubric's coming-soon rule and labelled none. Access is gated_partner because no self-serve credential path exists before the trial review.

name: Ecwid
one_liner: Embeddable ecommerce platform with a REST API for products, orders, and store data.

one_liner.note: Official Ecwid REST API reference for store data.

auth.note: All requests to Ecwid REST API require an access token. Ecwid uses OAuth 2.0 to provide secure access to the store data for public apps. If you customize your own store, you can skip OAuth and get a secret or public access token for your store and send it as a Bearer token.

External apps exchange a short-lived authorization code at https://my.ecwid.com/api/oauth/token/{store_id} with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, and client_secret, and receive a bearer access_token.
Access tokens are non-expiring authorization keys for REST API requests. A secret_token grants full access within the app permissions; a public_token is limited to public store data.

access.note: Only stores on paid plans can access API. You can sign up and create a custom application in the Ecwid admin to generate access tokens for your store. Ecwid can also email a free paid-plan upgrade for qualifying test stores, but buying a paid plan is a self-serve checkout path.
The plan comparison lists Ecwid REST API on Venture, Business, and Unlimited, not on Starter. Sign up, upgrade, or change your plan at any time from Ecwid admin, in My Profile → Billing and Plans.

api_surface.note: Official walkthrough of REST requests using store ID and a Bearer access token, starting with product and store-profile calls.
REST API overview and reference for Ecwid store objects.

mcp.note: Official Ecwid docs (including the documentation index) describe the REST API and app authentication, and do not publish an official MCP server URL or installable official MCP repo.

verdict.note: Public REST docs exist, and a developer can buy a paid plan online and create custom-app tokens with no human vendor review, so a toolkit can be built today.

notes: Custom-app secret and public tokens authenticate REST requests directly and are api_key. Public/external apps use OAuth 2.0; the app's client_secret is only for the token exchange, not a separate api_key. REST API starts on the Venture plan, which can be purchased in the admin, so access is self_serve_paid even if a later App Market listing is reviewed. No official MCP was found in official docs.
label_notes: Applied the clarified access rule: a self-serve custom-token path after buying a plan online keeps self_serve_paid, even if public OAuth / App Market apps may be reviewed. primary_auth is oauth2 because official docs document OAuth for public/third-party apps.

name: Apify
one_liner: Web scraping and automation platform for running Actors and accessing datasets through a REST API.

one_liner.note: The Apify API provides programmatic access to the Apify platform and is organized around RESTful HTTP endpoints.

auth.note: You can create an API token on the Integrations page in the Apify Console. To use your token in a request, add it to the Authorization header as Bearer <token> (recommended) or as the token query parameter.
To access the Apify API in your integrations, you need to authenticate using your secret API token. You manage your tokens on the API & Integrations page in Apify Console.

access.note: Create an API token in Apify Console under Settings > API & Integrations by selecting Create a new token. No vendor review is described.
Apify publishes a self-serve free plan and paid plans; API tokens are created in Console after signup.

api_surface.note: The Apify API (version 2) is organized around RESTful HTTP endpoints. The complete OpenAPI schema is available, and requests and responses are JSON.

mcp.note: The Apify MCP server (mcp.apify.com) allows AI applications and agents to interact with the Apify platform using Model Context Protocol. The hosted server is at https://mcp.apify.com. The recommended remote connection signs you in with OAuth; a Bearer API token is an alternative.

verdict.note: Public API docs and self-serve Console API tokens exist, so a toolkit can be built today.

notes: OAuth on the hosted MCP server is MCP authentication, not a documented method for calling the REST API, so it is not listed in auth_methods. The API reference also mentions agentic payments (x402 / Skyfire) as an alternative credential for some agent calls; that is noted here rather than treated as a general API auth method. Organization tokens may be issued by an account admin.
label_notes: api_key only for the developer API. Did not list oauth2 for MCP-only sign-in.

name: Vercel
one_liner: Frontend cloud platform for deploying web apps, with a REST API for projects, deployments, and teams.

one_liner.note: Official getting-started page for the Vercel REST API.

auth.note: Vercel access tokens authenticate requests to the Vercel REST API and the Vercel CLI on your behalf. You create and manage them on the Account Tokens page. Pass the token as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.
Vercel's IdP uses the OAuth 2.0 authorization framework. An Access Token is a bearer token your application uses to call the Vercel REST API for the permissions the user grants.

access.note: Create a Vercel API access token from your personal account's Account Tokens page by naming it, choosing a scope, and selecting Create. A Vercel account is the prerequisite; no vendor review is described.

api_surface.note: Example REST call: curl https://api.vercel.com/v9/projects with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Docs also cover deployments and token metadata endpoints.

mcp.note: Vercel MCP is Vercel's official MCP server. It's a remote MCP with OAuth available at https://mcp.vercel.com, including on all plans.

verdict.note: Public REST docs and self-serve access tokens exist, including OAuth tokens that call the same API, so a toolkit can be built today.

notes: Dashboard access tokens are api_key. Sign in with Vercel issues OAuth access tokens that call the REST API, so oauth2 is included and is primary_auth. MCP also uses OAuth, in addition to that API OAuth. Some teams require 2FA or SAML before creating team-scoped tokens; that is customer-side policy, not a vendor credential gate. Team or project installs need a user or admin to authorize.
label_notes: oauth2 is documented for calling the product API itself, not only MCP, so it is listed and preferred as primary_auth.

name: Harvest
one_liner: Time tracking and invoicing product with a REST API for time, projects, clients, and invoices.

one_liner.note: Harvest API V2 documentation for the time-tracking and invoicing API.

auth.note: The V2 API requires an access token to authenticate requests. There are two options: a Personal Access Token tied directly to you, or a full OAuth2 authentication flow which allows other people to use your Harvest integrations. Personal Access Tokens replace the Basic Authentication method that was used in v1.

access.note: Your Harvest subscription includes API access for all accounts (including free and trial accounts) which can be used to manage your Harvest account. All Harvest accounts are able to access the Harvest API.

api_surface.note: Example REST request to https://api.harvestapp.com/v2/users/me with Authorization: Bearer and Harvest-Account-Id headers.
Official API V2 overview for Harvest HTTP endpoints.

mcp.note: The official Harvest MCP is connected by setting the remote MCP server URL to https://api.harvestapp.com/mcp, then signing in to Harvest and authorizing the connection.

verdict.note: Public API docs and API access on free and trial accounts exist, so a toolkit can be built today.

notes: Personal Access Tokens are api_key. OAuth2 is documented for integrations other people can use, so it is primary_auth. The OAuth application secret is a client_secret, not a separate api_key. API permissions mirror the authorized Harvest user's role. A Harvest user must authorize the app or create a token in their account.
label_notes: Straightforward official docs. oauth2 plus PAT (api_key); no basic, because v1 Basic was replaced by tokens.

name: Binance
one_liner: Cryptocurrency exchange with a public REST API for market data, accounts, and trading.

one_liner.note: Public REST API for Binance, covering market data, trading, and account endpoints.

auth.note: Except for NONE, all endpoints with a security type are considered SIGNED requests (including a signature). Secure endpoints require a valid API key. SIGNED endpoints require an additional signature parameter, computed with HMAC, RSA, or Ed25519 keys.
Binance APIs require an API key to access authenticated endpoints. Supported key types are Ed25519 (recommended), HMAC, and RSA. HMAC keys are deprecated.

access.note: API keys can be created on the API Management page of your Binance account. By default, an API key cannot TRADE; you need to enable trading in API Management first. No vendor ticket or partner review is required to create keys.

api_surface.note: Official public REST API documentation for general, market data, trading, and account HTTP endpoints.

mcp.note: Official Binance MCP Server docs instruct clients to connect to https://agent.binance.com/mcp/agentic (for example: claude mcp add binance-mcp-server --transport http https://agent.binance.com/mcp/agentic) and then authenticate.
Binance Developer Docs describe the official MCP Server under Agent Native as the way to connect an AI agent to Binance.

verdict.note: Public REST docs and self-serve API Management keys exist, so a toolkit can be built today.

notes: Authenticated endpoints use a vendor-specific signed-request scheme (API key plus HMAC, RSA, or Ed25519 signature), labelled custom_other rather than a bare api_key. Public market-data endpoints have security type NONE. OAuth used to authorize the official MCP server is MCP authentication, not a documented method for the REST API, so it is not listed in auth_methods. Account identity checks may apply to some trading permissions, but keys are created by the account holder in API Management without a partner review. The official docs now live under developers.binance.com and the binance/binance-spot-api-docs repository; binance-docs.github.io is a stale hint.
label_notes: custom_other for the signed API-key scheme (HMAC/Ed25519/RSA). Did not list oauth2 for MCP-only authorization, and did not split api_key out as a second method because the key does not authenticate signed endpoints by itself.

name: Mermaid CLI
one_liner: Command-line tool that renders Mermaid diagram definitions to SVG, PNG, or PDF.

one_liner.note: This is a command-line interface (CLI) for mermaid. It takes a mermaid definition file as input and generates an SVG/PNG/PDF file as output.

auth.note: Install with npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli and run mmdc locally. No API key, OAuth, or hosted-service login is documented for the CLI itself.

access.note: The CLI is installable from npm and GitHub with no vendor review or paid credential step.

api_surface.note: Usage is the local mmdc command, for example mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.svg. Official mermaid docs redirect CLI users to this mermaid-cli repository.
mermaid CLI has been moved to mermaid-cli. Please read its documentation instead.

mcp.note: The official mermaid-js community integrations list includes MCP Server Mermaid (https://github.com/hustcc/mcp-mermaid) as a third-party MCP for generating Mermaid diagrams.
Community MCP server for generating Mermaid diagrams; not published as a mermaid-js first-party MCP for mermaid-cli.

verdict.note: A documented local CLI that can be wrapped as a skill is available to install immediately, with no hosted API required.

notes: This is the mermaid-js mermaid-cli tool, not Mermaid Chart (mermaid.ai). Mermaid Chart publishes a separate official MCP at mermaid.ai, which is a different product and is not used as mcp_url here. access is self_serve because the CLI is free to install and there are no vendor credentials; the interface is cli_only rather than no_public_api. Auth is none.
label_notes: Used the rubric exception that a local CLI wrapable as a skill is buildable_now. MCP is community (listed by mermaid-js as a community integration), not the Mermaid Chart official server.
